label: rem:chain-ring-energy
title: Hexagonalisation resistance of the C$_6$ chain
html:
Remark. Hexagonalisation resistance of the C_6 chain

The linear \mathrm{C}_6 chain and benzene represent two different topological states.

Energy accounting via Alexander polynomials. The crossing energy is proportional to the Alexander polynomial weight at the substrate parameter q:

Structure Binding topology \Delta(q) At q \approx 1
Chain \mathcal{C}_6 5 Hopf links 5 \times 1 5
Pairwise ring 6 Hopf links 6 \times 1 6
Threaded ring \mathcal{R}_6 T(2,6) q^2 + 1 + q^{-2} 3

The threaded ring binds 6 carbons with Alexander weight \approx 3, less than the chain's weight of 5.

Existence of the chain. The chain exists because the transition is discontinuous. It cannot continuously deform into the ring. The binding structure must dissolve, the atoms must reconfigure into a hexagon, and the threading link must form. This geometric reconfiguration is the activation barrier.

Once the threading forms, the energy drops below the chain. The threading link cannot be broken by a local perturbation.

Asymmetry of the barriers. The closure barrier is dominated by geometric reconfiguration. The opening barrier requires dissolving the threading link back into 5 separate Hopf links. This costs additional Alexander weight. Opening the ring is harder than closing it.
